raw_response:
I'll answer as the farmer would.

My old ways, I stick to them. I am 65, my wife and me, two old ones on 4.5 mu. Forty-five years I plant cotton here. I do what I know works.

Seed — I buy the Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town, same kind my neighbors buy. The bollworm doesn't eat it. About one and a half jin per mu. I don't try new kinds I haven't seen work in somebody else's field.

Land — after picking last fall I turned it over with the plough, deep. This spring I rake it smooth before planting. That's how we always do it.

Fertilizer — before planting I put down one bag of er'an (磷酸二铵, 50 kg) per mu, spread it and work it in. Then when the cotton is growing and starting to flower, I topdress one bag of urea (50 kg) per mu. That comes to about 30 jin of nitrogen per mu from the two together. Some years I also throw a little compound fertilizer if the plants look yellow. Fertilizer costs money, yes, but if I put too little the bolls will be small and I lose much more than I saved. Better a bit extra than short. My neighbor Old Wang puts about the same.

Water — I have the well. I water once before planting to wet the ground, once when it flowers in July, and once when the bolls are filling in August. Three times, unless the sky gives rain.

Spraying — cotton has many bugs. Aphids in early summer, then red spider, then whitefly later. I spray maybe five times through the season, whenever I see them on the leaves. I buy the medicine from the same shop.

Harvest — if the weather is normal and no big hail, I expect about 250 jin of seed cotton per mu. Some years better, some worse.
